info.title: Containarium API
info.description: Container management API for LXC-based development environments. Provides both gRPC and REST interfaces for managing containers, SSH keys, and system resources.

tags.name: ContainerService
tags.description: ContainerService provides container management operations

tags.name: SSHAuthzService
tags.description:
SSHAuthzService is the per-connection SSH authorization contract
(docs/architecture/ssh-live-authorization.md, component 1; #2516). The
sentinel's ssh-authz plugin asks the backend daemon, at connection time,
whether the credential offered may open a session as `login` on this
backend. The daemon answers from local state (self-host) or forwards to
the cloud over ActuationService.AuthorizeSSH, which reuses these same
messages so neither side translates.

The REST route is mounted behind the sentinel request signature
(auth.SentinelVerifier), not a JWT: it is sentinel-to-daemon plumbing.

tags.name: NetworkService
tags.description: NetworkService provides network and firewall management

tags.name: GuardrailEngineService
tags.description:
GuardrailEngineService is implemented by an ENGINE, not by the
Containarium daemon: the CLI (and later the daemon) is its client.
Stateless by contract — nothing is persisted on the engine side and
repeating a request repeats the scan. No REST mapping: this is an
internal plug point between two processes on the same side of a trust
boundary, not a product endpoint.

tags.name: GuardrailPolicyService
tags.description:
GuardrailPolicyService is the daemon's store for the server-side policy.
Get and GetStatus: any authenticated caller (a data owner needs the policy
to run `guardrail apply` against it). Set: admin role only, audited.

tags.name: RecipeService
tags.description:
RecipeService provides one-command deployment of declarative GPU/app
recipes onto Containarium backends.

tags.name: ModelGatewayService
tags.description:
ModelGatewayService is the control surface for the daemon's model gateway
(internal/modelgateway): who owns which upstream provider key, and the
short-lived scoped tokens a box presents instead of one.

The gateway's DATA plane is not here — it stays the HTTP proxy at
/v1/model/<provider> that a box calls with its gateway token. This service
is the admin + mint surface around it:

  - Set/Delete/GetStatus for one key owner's real upstream key. Admin-only
    (gateway:admin); the key goes in, and only a fingerprint ever comes back
    out. The keys live in the daemon's encrypted secrets store under a
    reserved namespace no tenant can list and no delivery mode ships into a
    box (internal/secrets.GatewayKeyLocation).
  - MintGatewayToken, which issues a scoped, revocable, short-lived token
    for a box the CALLER OWNS (gateway:mint). The token's key_owner claim —
    the box's cloud-org attribution when stamped, else its owning username —
    is what makes the call spend that owner's upstream key rather than the
    daemon operator's.
  - ListGatewayModels, the upstream model list read through the gateway, so
    a caller can see what it may ask for without ever holding a real key.

Design: docs/architecture/workspace-own-inference-key.md (cloud repo),
component 2 / contract C1.

tags.name: ProofPackService
tags.description:
ProofPackService verifies a sealed Proof Pack from a client (#3064), so a
caller that is not on the daemon host (where `containarium proof-pack
verify` reads Postgres directly) can check one.

tags.name: AgentSkillService
tags.description: AgentSkillService manages and runs individual packaged agents.

tags.name: CrewService
tags.description: CrewService runs collaborating sets of skills bound to a task purpose.

tags.name: AnonymousBoxService
tags.description:
AnonymousBoxService is the daemon side of the `ssh new.<cloud-domain>`
door (docs/architecture/ssh-new-anonymous-box.md): a Linux VM per SSH
key fingerprint, no account required, claimable into a tenant by
signing up, destroyed at TTL otherwise. The sentinel's door plugin calls
EnsureAnonymousBox; the cloud control plane (or an admin) calls
ClaimAnonymousBox; everything else is operator surface.

tags.name: AppService
tags.description: AppService provides application deployment and management

tags.name: SentinelSSHBanService
tags.description:
SentinelSSHBanService controls the enforcing plugin, not system fail2ban.
The sentinel mounts REST behind its admin HMAC and forwards to a local socket.

tags.name: AuditService
tags.description:
AuditService — the proto-defined surface of the tamper-evident audit
store (internal/audit). Today it carries one write RPC (#2415): the
sentinel ships the SSH session records its sshpiperd plugin appends
locally (internal/sentinel/sshsession) into THIS backend's audit chain,
so the platform's front-door logins get the same hash chain and
external anchoring (#1706) as in-box sessions and API calls.

Reads stay on the legacy /v1/audit/logs gateway route for now.

tags.name: BackupService
tags.description:
BackupService provides logical (pg_dump) database backups for the
databases running inside Containarium containers, stored off-host.
See docs/DB-BACKUP-OPERATIONS.md for the operational runbook and the
ISO 27001 A.8.13 control mapping.

tags.name: SandboxService
tags.description:
SandboxService is the two-digit-ms spawn path
(docs/architecture/two-digit-ms-sandbox-spawn.md): an isolated Linux
process for an agent inner loop, claimed against a pool rather than
created fresh per request.

A sandbox is NOT a persistent box. It has no per-tenant Linux account and
no SSH — access is exclusively these RPCs, over a connection the daemon
already holds open. That is the scope cut that makes the latency target
reachable (see the design note's "What's in it" section); a caller that
needs `ssh <user>@box` wants ContainerService instead.

Phase 1 (this contract's first implementation) is the cold path only —
every SpawnSandbox call creates a fresh container, same floor as
ContainerService.CreateContainer minus identity seeding. served_from is
always COLD until Phase 3 adds the warm pool; the field exists now so
that Phase 3 is not a breaking proto change.

tags.name: SpawnService
tags.description:
SpawnService is agent-box's resident, low-latency counterpart to
SandboxService's per-call Incus round-trips (#1488 Phase 2). Each Incus
exec websocket-upgrades at ~50-150ms; a warm gRPC connection straight to
the box does the same work in ~3ms. The daemon reaches this over a
bind-mounted unix socket (see the design note's "Transport" section),
never over the network.

This is deliberately the only service in this package with NO
google.api.http annotations: it is not part of the public API surface —
SandboxService is what external callers (CLI, MCP, SDK) talk to, and its
implementation is what will route through SpawnService once a warm pool
exists (Phase 3). Nothing here is reachable through the REST gateway,
and it must not be registered there.

agent-box runs as PID 1 inside a pool member (see the design note's flow
diagram), so it owns reaping every process it forks — a design this
service inherits from the existing process_start/shell_exec MCP tools in
internal/agentbox, not a new mechanism.

tags.name: ClusterService
tags.description:
ClusterService manages tenant-facing managed Kubernetes clusters (#1413).

A managed cluster is a platform-operated k3s control plane plus worker
nodes that are Containarium VMs, grouped into typed size classes the
cluster-autoscaler expands by fit simulation. The tenant's only surface
is this service and the kubeconfig it returns — the control-plane VM is
platform territory (no tenant SSH, absent from the tenant's container
list), and worker VMs are cluster-internal.

Design: docs/architecture/managed-k8s-clusters.md. Provisioning is
asynchronous: CreateCluster records the desired cluster and returns; a
daemon-side reconciler (#1414) converges VMs and flips the cluster to
READY. Kubeconfig and node-join material are read on demand from the
control-plane VM and are never persisted by the platform.

tags.name: CodingToolEgressPolicyService
tags.description:
CodingToolEgressPolicyService — the admin-approved egress allowlist for the
coding CLI's own traffic (#2370, docs/architecture/coding-cli-egress-allowlist.md).

Separate from NetworkPolicyService on purpose: a coding-tool policy never
changes what a tenant's own NetworkPolicy means. This service is the policy
store only; the kernel-side enforcement is a later increment.

tags.name: TrafficService
tags.description: TrafficService provides container traffic monitoring capabilities

tags.name: ThreatDetectionService
EventService
tags.description: EventService provides real-time event streaming

tags.name: KmsService
tags.description:
KmsService exposes read + migration-trigger operations for the
tenant-secrets envelope-encryption layer (see
docs/security/KMS-ENVELOPE-DESIGN.md). It deliberately does NOT
expose backend *configuration* — selecting a KMS backend and
supplying its credentials stays an operator/systemd concern
(CONTAINARIUM_KMS_BACKEND + the per-backend env vars), never an
over-the-wire action. Every RPC requires the `kms:admin` scope
AND the admin role; these are platform-wide, not tenant-scoped.

tags.name: NetworkPolicyService
tags.description:
NetworkPolicyService — the control-plane CRUD for per-tenant network
isolation policies (Phase A of the eBPF network-isolation design, #315).

This is the policy *store* surface: operators (and the cloud control plane)
set/get/list/delete a tenant's NetworkPolicy here; the per-veth TC_INGRESS
BPF loader (a later increment) consumes the stored policies and programs the
kernel. Admin-only — policies are fleet-shaping config, not tenant-editable.

tags.name: NotifyService
tags.description:
NotifyService — where the daemon pushes a `code run --approvals ask`
permission request that is waiting on the developer (#2185,
docs/product/phone-approval.md Story 3).

One channel per user. The daemon itself sends the push: it reads each live
run's input journal on the user's box and publishes to the channel, so the
channel's access token never reaches a box. The token is stored with the
tenant secrets store as a broker-only secret named
CONTAINARIUM_NOTIFY_NTFY_TOKEN_<random>, a new one per token (the channel
switches to it in one write), and is never returned by any RPC.

Which user: the request's username, or the caller's own when empty. Reads
need secrets:read and writes secrets:write, as for the tenant's secrets.

tags.name: PentestService
tags.description: PentestService provides automated penetration testing and vulnerability scanning

tags.name: RetentionService
tags.description:
RetentionService stores the retention policy and legal holds and reports
what a sweep would remove. Every RPC is
admin-only. A set, a hold and a release write an audit entry naming the
caller when the daemon has an audit store; a failed audit write fails the
change and leaves the store unchanged.

tags.name: SecurityService
tags.description: SecurityService provides container security scanning and reporting

tags.name: SentinelSSHUpstreamService
tags.description:
SentinelSSHUpstreamService is private to the local operator's Unix socket.
It is never registered on public gRPC or REST listeners.

tags.name: TokensService
tags.description:
TokensService is the admin surface for JWT lifecycle.

RevokeToken requires an admin role + tokens:write scope;
tenants can't revoke other tenants' tokens. RefreshToken
is open to any holder of a valid refresh token — that's
the whole point of the exchange flow.

tags.name: TrackerService
tags.description:
TrackerService manages tracker connections — the daemon-custody seam
the tracker broker's issue/change-request verbs (#1922, #1923) build
on. Connection CRUD is gated by tracker:admin, deliberately separate
from the tracker:read / tracker:write scopes an agent's run-scoped JWT
carries for the verbs themselves: naming where the tracker is and
which credential to trust is an operator decision, not something a
skill run should be able to change.

tags.name: VolumeService
tags.description:
VolumeService manages shared, multi-writer data volumes (#384).

The only storage mechanism that lets N containers mount the SAME volume
read-write without corruption is a CephFS custom (filesystem) volume:
CephFS's MDS + capability/lease protocol coordinates concurrent POSIX
writers, which a block device on a non-cluster filesystem (ext4/xfs/zfs)
cannot. So this service is capability-gated: it only works on hosts
backed by a `cephfs` Incus storage pool, and rejects create/attach on
single-node ZFS hosts (today's default) with a clear error. Callers
check support via ListVolumes.shared_volumes_supported.

NOTE: this is a single-writer-safe DATA volume, not an instance rootfs
(Incus restricts the cephfs driver to custom volumes).

tags.name: ZapService
tags.description: ZapService provides OWASP ZAP web application security scanning

get.summary: Page through current bans on one independently enforcing listener.

parameters.name: pageToken
parameters.description: Last returned normalized IP; iteration is in lexical IP order.

post.summary: Atomically clear exactly one source's counter and ban; admin-only.

get.summary: Inspect one source IP, including tracked, banned, and exempt states.

post.summary:
ReportContainerState records the calling host's observed state
for one of its assigned containers. The cloud uses this to
surface the user-facing containers.state field and (in a future
slice) to react to FAILED reports with reassignment.
post.description:
Errors:
  - InvalidArgument: malformed container_id, empty / unknown state.
  - NotFound: no live assignment for that container belongs to
    the calling host. Single error code for "container unknown"
    and "container is on a different host" — the calling host
    can't distinguish, by design.
  - Unauthenticated: missing / invalid host-bearer.

parameters.name: containerId
parameters.description:
The container the host is reporting about. The host must hold a
live container_assignments row for this container; cross-host
reports collapse to NotFound for probe resistance (the calling
host can't tell whether the container exists on another host).

post.summary:
EnrollHost redeems a single-use join token and registers the BYO host.
Self-authenticating via the token in the body (NOT host-bearer — the row
doesn't exist yet).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
EnrollHostRequest carries the single-use join token a BYO host redeems to
register itself with the cloud (BYO-compute report path). Unlike every other
ActuationService RPC this one is NOT host-bearer authed — the host row
doesn't exist yet; the cloud validates + single-use-redeems the token.

post.summary:
Heartbeat updates hosts.last_heartbeat_at for the calling host.
A stale gap (>2 × the host's expected interval) marks the host
for the HostSweeper, which reassigns its containers. Hosts are
expected to call this every N seconds with N << the staleness
threshold.
post.description:
Auth: requires a valid `host-bearer` header. Returns
Unauthenticated if missing / malformed / tombstoned. The
method is otherwise idempotent.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
HeartbeatRequest is intentionally empty for v1. The host's identity
comes from the bearer; there's nothing else the cloud needs to
know to bump last_heartbeat_at. Future fields (current observed
state, host-side health flags) are additive.

get.summary:
GetSSHTrustBundle returns what this host needs to trust the cloud's SSH
CA and refuse revoked certificates: the CA public keys for sshd's
TrustedUserCAKeys, and a KRL spec for RevokedKeys.
get.description:
Auth: requires a valid `host-bearer` header — the same channel the host
already uses for enrollment and heartbeats, so no new transport, no new
credential, and nothing for an operator to wire up per host.

Errors:
  - Unauthenticated: missing / invalid host-bearer.
  - Unimplemented: this daemon has no SSH CA configured.

parameters.name: knownVersion
parameters.description:
Optional. The version the caller already has applied. When it matches
the current one the response sets `unchanged` and omits the payload, so
a frequent poll costs almost nothing.

post.summary:
ReportHostStatus upserts the calling host's capability profile +
`doctor` self-check and bumps its heartbeat. Requires a valid
`host-bearer` header. Idempotent.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
ReportHostStatusRequest is a BYO host's push of its self-measured
capability profile + `doctor` self-check. Host-bearer authed; the host id
comes from the bearer, never the body.

get.summary: List agent engines and their readiness
get.description: Returns one row per agent engine: whether a skill naming it would be refused right now, why, and which catalog skills name it explicitly.
Returns one byte window of a run member's journal plus the offset to resume from. Resumable across dropped connections; follow_seconds waits briefly for new bytes.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The run to read: a RunAgentSkill run id or a RunCrew run id.

parameters.name: skillId
parameters.description:
Which member's journal to read. Empty = the only member of a skill run,
or the entry skill (first member) of a crew run.

parameters.name: startOffset
parameters.description:
Byte offset to start reading from; 0 = from the beginning. Pass the
previous response's end_offset to resume without loss or repetition.

parameters.name: maxBytes
parameters.description: Upper bound on chunk size in bytes: <= 262144; 0 means 65536.

parameters.name: followSeconds
parameters.description:
0..10: when no bytes are available at start_offset, wait up to this many
seconds for the journal to grow before answering with an empty chunk.

parameters.name: gatewayAfterSeq
parameters.description:
Model-gateway calls recorded for this run and member after this sequence
number (#2928); 0 = from the first. Pass the previous response's
gateway_next_seq to resume. Independent of start_offset: the calls are
recorded by the daemon, not written to the journal file.

get.description: Returns all packaged agent skills that can be run individually or composed into a crew.
Returns one skill's definition, including its agent card, allowed scopes, and allowed peers.

get.summary: Check a skill box's coding-agent credential source
get.description: Reports the NAME of the credential source (interactive sign-in, a user-placed key, or none) the skill's box would use for its configured engine — never the credential's value, never read/logged/transmitted.

post.summary: Provision a skill's box ahead of any run
post.description: Creates or reuses the skill's deterministic box with no token minted, nothing seeded, and no model call — so a human can sign in to its coding agent before any inference credential exists.
Provisions the skill's box, mints a scoped token, runs one task, and returns the artifact.

post.summary: Start a pull-queue worker for a skill
post.description: Provisions the skill's box, mints an agents:run queue credential, and launches the in-box runtime in poll mode to lease and run queued tasks.

parameters.name: skillId
parameters.description:
Skill whose box runs as the worker (its persona is the worker's; the
worker leases only this skill's tasks).

post.summary: Send a task to a peer agent (A2A)
post.description: Delegates a task to a running peer agent over the agent-to-agent transport and returns the peer's artifact.

parameters.name: toPeerId
parameters.description: The target peer to deliver the task to.

post.description: Places a task on the pull queue for a skill; worker boxes lease and run it.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: EnqueueAgentTaskRequest places one task on the pull queue.

post.summary: Lease the next agent task (pull queue)
post.description: Worker boxes poll this to lease the next task; the task is hidden from other workers until completed or the lease expires.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: LeaseAgentTaskRequest asks for the next runnable task.

post.summary: Complete a leased agent task (pull queue)
post.description: Worker boxes report a leased task's artifact/error here; a stale lease is rejected.

get.description: Returns all custom alert rules stored in the database.

post.description: Creates a new custom alert rule. The rule is persisted in PostgreSQL and synced to vmalert for evaluation.

get.description: Returns the built-in default alert rules for system and container monitoring. These rules are always active and cannot be modified.
Returns a single alert rule by its ID.

delete.description: Deletes an alert rule by ID. The rule is removed from both the database and vmalert.

put.description: Updates an existing alert rule. Changes are synced to vmalert automatically.

get.description: Every live anonymous box with its fingerprint hash, expiry and claim state. Admin only.

post.description: Bind an anonymous box to a tenant using its claim token. Admin / control plane only.
Resolve or create the anonymous VM for an SSH public key. Sentinel door / admin only.

get.description: Kill switch, bans and the fixed per-box limits of the anonymous tier. Admin only.

put.description: Enable/disable the anonymous door and edit banned fingerprints. Admin only.

get.description: Returns a list of deployed applications with optional filtering by state or username.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username (empty for all - admin only)

parameters.name: stateFilter
parameters.description:
Filter by state

 - APP_STATE_UNSPECIFIED: Unspecified state (should not be used)
 - APP_STATE_UPLOADING: Source code is being uploaded
 - APP_STATE_BUILDING: Container image is being built (using Podman)
 - APP_STATE_RUNNING: App is running and healthy
 - APP_STATE_STOPPED: App is stopped by user
 - APP_STATE_FAILED: Build or runtime failure
 - APP_STATE_RESTARTING: App is restarting

post.description: Deploys a new application or updates an existing one. Accepts source code + Dockerfile/Containerfile or auto-detects language and generates one.

get.description: Returns detailed information about a specific application including state, domain, and configuration.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

delete.description: Permanently deletes an application and optionally removes associated data volumes.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

parameters.name: removeData
parameters.description: Remove persistent data volumes

get.description: Returns application logs with optional streaming. Use follow=true for real-time log streaming.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

parameters.name: tailLines
parameters.description: Number of lines from end (default: 100)

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Stream logs (Server-Sent Events)

post.description: Restarts an application by stopping and starting it.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

post.description: Starts a stopped application.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

post.description: Stops a running application. The application can be started again later.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username

parameters.name: appName
parameters.description: App name

post.description: Append sentinel SSH session open/close records to this backend's tamper-evident audit chain. Idempotent per (session_id, phase); all-or-nothing per batch. Requires the audit:ingest scope.

get.description: Lists every backend in the fleet (local daemon + tunnel peers) with health, version, OS, running container count, and GPU inventory. Admin-only — discloses fleet topology.

post.summary: Trigger daemon upgrade on a backend
post.description: Upgrades a backend's daemon to the binary the sentinel currently serves, immediately instead of on the periodic tick. SHA-verified and smoke-tested before an atomic swap; the daemon restarts. Admin-only. Returns an upgrade_id for GetUpgradeStatus.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
TriggerUpgradeRequest asks a backend to upgrade its daemon binary now instead
of waiting for the periodic auto-update tick. The daemon pulls the binary the
sentinel currently serves (SHA-verified), smoke-tests it, swaps atomically
(keeping the previous binary as .old), and restarts. See #354 Phase B.

get.description: Lists stored backup records (newest first), optionally filtered by tenant.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description:
Optional tenant filter. Empty lists backups for all tenants
(admin view).

post.description: Runs pg_dump inside the tenant's container and stores the dump at the chosen off-host destination (local backup dir or GCS). Leave connection.database empty to back up every non-template database found; set it to back up just one. scope=BACKUP_SCOPE_BOX backs up the whole box instead: no connection or hook, and an explicit encryption key_mode is required.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
CreateBackupRequest dumps a container's database and stores it at the
chosen destination.

post.summary: Prune old backups, keeping the newest N per database
post.description: Deletes older backup records for a tenant, keeping the newest `keep` per (username, database) — or per (username, label) for a hook backup. One failing delete never aborts pruning the rest. #1839.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
PruneBackupsRequest deletes older backups for a tenant, keeping only the
newest `keep` per (username, database) group — or per (username, label)
for a `--hook` backup, since a hook backup's label fills the same
database field (#1839). Retention POLICY (when, how often, how many) is
still the caller's decision; this RPC is the mechanism that makes
"how many" actually enforceable instead of a cron job hand-rolling
`rm` against the daemon's backup directory.

get.description: Returns the metadata for a single stored backup.

delete.description: Deletes a stored dump and its metadata by id. See PruneBackups for keep-newest-N retention instead of naming ids one at a time.

post.description: Streams a stored dump back into a container's database via pg_restore. Destructive when clean=true.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Backup to restore. A SNAPSHOT backup restarts its source box on a new
PVC in the same namespace, retaining the old PVC. connection, clean,
age_identity and target_container must be unset for snapshot restores.

post.description: Restore-tests a stored dump by loading it into a throwaway database inside a target container and running sanity checks, then dropping the scratch database. Never touches the source container. An encrypted backup needs age_identity to decrypt; a wrong identity comes back as a FAILED result, not an error. Records the outcome on the backup as durable A.8.13 evidence.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Backup to verify.

get.description: Returns a backend's last-recorded capability profile (hardware class, GPU probe, micro-benchmark, region) without re-running it. Admin-only.

parameters.name: backendId
parameters.description: Backend to read. Empty = the local/primary daemon's own host.

post.description: Records a backend's capability profile (hardware class, GPU probe, bounded CPU/memory micro-benchmark, region) and reconciles measured vs self-reported class. Surfaced through ListBackends. Admin-only.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
ProfileBackendRequest asks a backend to (re)record its capability profile:
read system info, run the GPU passthrough probe and the bounded
CPU/memory micro-benchmark, derive the measured class, and persist it. See
#681.

get.description: Returns this backend's current headroom advertisement and recomputed spare figures. Admin-only.

delete.description: Withdraws this backend's headroom advertisement. Idempotent — succeeds even when nothing is currently advertised. Admin-only.

parameters.name: drain
parameters.description:
When true the backend also reclaims the guest workloads it had implicitly
offered, draining them gracefully within a bounded window instead of
hard-killing them. Each drained workload is stopped through the normal
stop path so the control plane observes a stop event and can reschedule.
When false (default) withdraw only flips the advertisement off and leaves
running guests untouched. See #682.

parameters.name: drainWindowSeconds
parameters.description:
Bounded wall-clock budget (seconds) for the graceful drain. Once exhausted
any still-running candidate is force-stopped so the host is reliably
reclaimed (no wedge on repeated advertise/withdraw cycles). 0 applies the
backend default (120s). Only honored when drain is true.

post.description: Publishes this backend's spare scheduling headroom (spare CPU/memory/disk + host idle fraction) to the control plane, bounded by a local policy. Surfaced through ListBackends. Admin-only.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
AdvertiseCapacityRequest publishes (or republishes) this backend's spare
scheduling headroom to the control plane, bounded by the supplied policy.
See #680.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description:
Owner filter. Non-admin callers may only list their own clusters;
empty = the authenticated caller (admins: all clusters).

post.description: Records the cluster and returns immediately in state PROVISIONING; a reconciler provisions the control-plane and worker VMs asynchronously. Fails fast on hosts that cannot run VMs.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owning tenant. Empty = the authenticated caller.

delete.description: Tears down control-plane and worker VMs, the published API endpoint, and all cluster state. A re-created cluster of the same name starts empty.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owning tenant. Empty = the authenticated caller.

get.description: Only available once the cluster is READY. The kubeconfig is read from the control-plane VM on each call and is not persisted by the platform.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owning tenant. Empty = the authenticated caller.

get.description: Control-plane health, per-node-group counts vs min/max, and the most recent scale events with reasons.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Owning tenant. Empty = the authenticated caller.

parameters.name: eventsLimit
parameters.description: Max scale events to return, newest first. 0 = server default (20).

get.description: Return the stored and effective coding-tool egress policy. On GET /v1/code/egress-policy/{tenant} the tenant is the URL value; on the bare GET /v1/code/egress-policy it is the optional ?tenant= query parameter, and with none the cluster default (admin only). Admin, or the tenant itself holding the code-egress:read scope.

put.description: Makes the container user's authorized_keys contain exactly the given public keys. Keys not in the list are removed; keys the platform manages itself (the sentinel's upstream key) are never removed. Idempotent. The file is rewritten, not edited: each kept key is written as a regenerated canonical line (comment reduced to a safe charset), and comment lines, unparseable lines and any other line not in the list are dropped. At most 100 keys of 8 KB each. A dropped key is always removed from this container user's file. Its ssh_keys registry entry is handled as RemoveSSHKey does: one entry per key, owned by the first account to register it, until that entry is revoked, after which the next registration replaces it (an owner account also owns an entry its own collaborator account <owner>-container-<user> registered, since ownership compares user id); it is revoked when this container user owns it or it has no owner, and no other account (a collaborator account is a separate account) still holds the same public key in its own authorized_keys. A key another account holds is dropped from this file but its entry stays active, and the call still succeeds; if this container user owned the entry, the entry loses its owner, so the next account to register the key takes it over and the last holder's own drop revokes it. When another account owns the entry it stays active, so dropping a key is not a guaranteed revocation of a compromised key. Dropped keys are revoked before the file changes, so a registry failure leaves the file untouched and a retry repeats the revocation. An empty list removes every caller-managed key and must be requested with allow_empty=true. Every key must be a single-line public key with no authorized_keys options; one invalid key fails the whole call with no change. Requires the same access as AddSSHKey.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username of the container

delete.description: Removes an SSH public key from a container's authorized_keys file, revoking that key's SSH access to this container. The key's ssh_keys registry entry (one per key, owned by the first account to register it; a revoked entry is replaced by the next registration) is revoked when this container user owns it or it has no owner. Ownership compares user id, so an owner account also owns an entry its own collaborator account <owner>-container-<user> registered on another box. If this call would revoke the entry but any other account (a collaborator account <owner>-container-<collab> is a separate account here) still holds the same public key in its own authorized_keys, the key is removed from this container user's file only and the entry stays active; the call still succeeds and does not say which account holds the key. If this container user owned that entry, the entry loses its owner: the next account to register the key takes it over, and the last holder's own removal revokes it. A key whose entry another account owns is likewise removed from the file with the entry left active, so removing a key is not a guaranteed revocation of a compromised key. The revocation happens before the file changes, so a registry failure leaves the key in place and a retry repeats it. The ssh_public_key should be URL-encoded.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username of the container

parameters.description: SSH public key to remove (exact match)

put.summary: Set the baseline response scan mode
put.description: Switch the baseline response scan between LOG (default: stream unchanged, scan at the end, audit a match) and BLOCK (hold the response, block a match). Stored separately from the server policy, so it never turns the baseline off; it applies only while no policy is configured. UNSPECIFIED is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Increments the setting's revision. On a daemon with an audit store it writes an audit entry naming the caller, and if that write fails the switch fails with INTERNAL and the mode is unchanged; with no audit store (no Postgres, REST disabled, or an audit store that failed to start) the switch succeeds and writes no entry. get.description: Return the cluster-wide guardrail policy, its trusted signers, revision and policy hash. configured=false when no policy was ever set. Any authenticated caller.

put.description: Replace the cluster-wide guardrail policy and trusted signers. A request that drops or changes a stored revoked key is FAILED_PRECONDITION (revocation is permanent); an expected_revision that is not the stored revision is ABORTED. Increments the revision and writes an audit entry. Admin role only.

get.summary: Get the effective response guardrail policy
